# Pawsfect pilot structured interview scorecard

**Status:** review draft only. Do not use until classification, role policy,
screening process, interview process, insurance and owner authorization gates
are verified. Store completed scorecards only in the approved private system.

Use the same core questions, follow-up boundaries and anchored scale for every
person considered for the same approved role. Interviewers record observable,
job-related evidence—not impressions about personality or protected traits.

## Anchored scale

| Score | Evidence standard |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | No relevant example, unsafe answer or unwilling to follow the approved boundary. |
| 1 | Partial example; material gap remains and no safe escalation path is described. |
| 2 | Clear relevant example with a safe action, communication and escalation path. |

No single total automatically creates an offer. Before use, the owner must set
and document consistent decision rules and any safety-critical minimums in the
private interview policy.

## Core questions

| Competency | Ask every candidate | Strong evidence to listen for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Safe handling | “Tell us about a time a dog became fearful, over-aroused or difficult to control. What did you do?” | Creates distance, avoids punishment/escalation, follows the care plan, stops when unsafe and promptly communicates. |
| Care-plan discipline | “Describe how you would prepare for and complete a first visit using written household instructions.” | Confirms scope and access, checks ambiguity before acting, stays within authorization and closes the visit securely. |
| Judgment | “Weather or an unexpected condition makes the planned walk unsafe. Walk us through your decision.” | Prioritizes animal/person safety, uses the approved exception process, documents facts and does not improvise an excluded service. |
| Reliability | “Give an example of preventing or handling a late arrival or missed commitment.” | Plans ahead, communicates early, uses escalation/backup rules and takes responsibility without exposing private details. |
| Privacy and trust | “How would you handle keys, entry instructions, client information and photos?” | Least access, approved tools only, no personal reuse/sharing, prompt incident reporting and return/deletion under policy. |
| Emergency response | “You notice an injury or a dog slips equipment. What are your first actions?” | Secures immediate safety if possible, follows the emergency/lost-dog plan, contacts the designated channel and records objective facts. |
| Scope boundaries | “A client asks for transportation, medication or an off-leash activity outside the approved visit. What do you do?” | Declines or pauses, explains the authorization boundary and escalates instead of accepting side work. |
| Communication | “Explain how you would report an unusual but non-emergency event after a visit.” | Timely, factual, concise, privacy-aware report through the approved channel without diagnosis or blame. |

## Consistent follow-ups

Interviewers may ask “What happened next?”, “What was your responsibility?” and
“What would you do differently?” They must not investigate protected traits,
medical/genetic information, family plans, religion, national origin, unrelated
arrest/financial history or other non-job-related personal information.

## Decision and escalation controls

- A trained reviewer checks completeness and consistency before any decision.
- Any background-report step occurs only under the separately approved consent,
  notice and dispute process—never during an informal interview.
- References, licenses or driving information are requested only if the final
  role policy establishes a job-related need and an approved private workflow.
- Safety concerns are recorded as objective role evidence, not public notes.
- Offers, agreements, compensation and start dates require a separate
  owner-authorized process; this scorecard does not authorize them.
